question: Using determinants, calculate the area of the triangle whose vertices are $(1,2)$, $(4,6)$ and $(7,2)$. Also examine whether the vertices are collinear.
explanation:
Determinant form of the area
The area is $$\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}1&2&1\\4&6&1\\7&2&1\end{vmatrix}\right|$$
Expansion of the determinant
Its value is $$1(6-2)-2(4-7)+(8-42)$$
Simplification
Therefore, the determinant equals $$4+6-34=-24$$ Hence, the area is $$\frac{1}{2}|-24|=12$$ square units.
Collinearity examination
The area is nonzero, so the three vertices are not collinear.
Thus, the triangle has area $12$ square units.

options.A: Area $=6$ square units; the vertices are not collinear.
options.B: Area $=12$ square units; the vertices are collinear.
options.C: Area $=12$ square units; the vertices are not collinear.
options.D: Area $=24$ square units; the vertices are not collinear.
